definitions.explanation: Applicable to or affecting all people, places, or situations without exception. Describes values, truths, or phenomena that are not limited to a particular culture, era, or group.

examples.japanese: {愛|あい}は{普遍的|ふへんてき}なテーマだ。
{人権|じんけん}は{普遍的|ふへんてき}な{価値|かち}である。
examples.english: Human rights are a universal value.

examples.japanese: この{物語|ものがたり}は{時代|じだい}を{超|こ}えた{普遍的|ふへんてき}な{魅力|みりょく}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: This story has a universal appeal that transcends time.

notes:
{普遍的|ふへんてき} describes something that applies to or affects all people, places, or situations without exception.

WORD FORMATION:
{普遍|ふへん} (universality) + {的|てき} (adjectival suffix). The base noun {普遍|ふへん} also exists and means "universality."

FORMS:
- Na-adjective: {普遍的|ふへんてき}な{価値|かち} (universal value)
- Adverbial: {普遍的|ふへんてき}に{当|あ}てはまる (applies universally)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {普遍的|ふへんてき}な{価値|かち}: universal value
- {普遍的|ふへんてき}な{真理|しんり}: universal truth
- {普遍的|ふへんてき}なテーマ: universal theme
- {普遍的|ふへんてき}な{原理|げんり}: universal principle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一般的|いっぱんてき}: general (less absolute than universal)
- {共通|きょうつう}: common, shared (more everyday)
- {万国共通|ばんこくきょうつう}: common to all nations

REGISTER:
Formal/academic. Common in philosophy, law, and intellectual discourse. In casual speech, みんなに{当|あ}てはまる (applies to everyone) is more natural.
